subject: MedShore: phased backup purge plan + DPA subprocessors & transfer map
messages:
From: Natalie Ramos <natalie.ramos@medshore.health>

Cc: MedShore Legal <legal@medshore.health>

Subject: Backup purge timing + DPA subprocessors & transfer map

Hi Laura,

We're finalizing our DPA amendment with Procurement and need Redwood's input to close out a few items:

- Proposed phased purge timeline for customer backups (MedShore requires clarity on when backups are eligible for purge).
- Canonical list of subprocessors involved in backups & logs and the countries where those subprocessors operate.
- Any cross-border transfer map (even high level) and whether you anticipate needing SCCs or other transfer mechanisms for specific subprocs.

Procurement has two competing asks: a 90-day backup retention expectation to match our app SLA, and a secondary ask from Legal for a 180-day hold for certain classes of data. We want to avoid multiple document cycles—can you provide: a recommended phased approach, required DPA language (or redline), and whether Redwood can produce deletion evidence for purged backups?

I've attached our initial inventory export to help (inventory is partial). Happy to schedule a quick call if preferable.

Thanks,
Natalie Ramos
VP, Infrastructure & Security
MedShore Health

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Backup purge timing + DPA subprocessors & transfer map

Hi Natalie — thanks for the clear ask and the inventory.

Short answer: we can support a phased purge cadence that satisfies both Procurement and Legal, plus provide deletion attestations for purges with a defined evidence package. Initial proposal below (high level):

Phase proposal (recommended):
- Days 0–30: Hot backups / immediate restore window (low-latency, frequent snapshots; retention enforced).
- Days 31–90: Warm hold — backups moved to lower-cost storage but still available for restore within SLA (72 hrs typical).
- Days 91–180: Cold hold — archived snapshots retained for compliance; restores permitted but require approval and 7–14 day prep.
- Post-180: Purge candidate. Purge executed in staged waves by subprocessor and retention class. Full deletion evidence (checksum summary + deletion log) produced per wave.

Notes/asks:
- We need MedShore to identify any legal hold carveouts (e.g., ongoing litigation, HIPAA-related holds).
- Please confirm whether Procurement's 90-day requirement is mandatory for all data classes or only for production transactional data.

Next steps: I will draft a short DPA amendment blurb and a purge-runbook checklist for your review. Kim, can you list the current backup/log subprocessors and countries here so we can produce the transfer map? Markus, please confirm restore SLA options & typical evidence artifacts. Aditya, flag any marketplace/contracting implications (DocuSign/hubspot links).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Backup purge timing + DPA subprocessors & transfer map

Laura — adding the subproc list & a few clarifications:

Current subprocessors impacting backups/logs:
- AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2) — primary object store for snapshots.
- FastCache Inc. (US) — in-memory KV caching used in live workloads; not a long-term backup store but appears in inventory metadata.
- SubProcLogs Ltd. (Ireland) — long-term cold log archival (encrypted at rest).
- GlacierPartner (US) — archival tier used for 120+ day snapshots.

Country notes: AWS regions are US; SubProcLogs Ltd is in IE (EU). That implies we have cross-border flows from EU logs to US-based restore processes for some admin tools — we should render a simple transfer map and highlight the need for SCCs if MedShore requires EU->US specific contractual safeguards.

Log-retention exception path (short):
1) Customer requests exception via Trust request form (security@redwood.ai).
2) Engineering evaluates feasibility & operational risk (48h SLA to respond).
3) Exception escalated to Legal for approval if >90 days or involves cross-border transfer concerns.

I'll attach a CSV export separately with subproc names and contact emails.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Operations

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Backup purge timing + DPA subprocessors & transfer map

Hi Natalie — following up with technical details on the purge waves and restore SLA options. I've also dropped a draft DPA amendment link for Legal to iterate.

Purge execution details (example):
- Wave 1 (by day 190): Purge ephemeral snapshots (non-customer artifacts) — immediate delete across object store + kv metadata scrub.
- Wave 2 (by day 200): Purge cold archives in GlacierPartner — archival index updated, then deletion job triggered (multi-pass to ensure eventual consistency).
- Wave 3 (by day 210): Final metadata sweep and removal of any auxiliary logs tied to purged snapshots.

Restore SLAs:
- Standard: 72 hours (applies to warm hold).
- Legal/forensic restores: 7–14 days (requires approval and scheduled retrieval from archive).

Evidence package (what Redwood provides when purge executed):
- Deletion job id + timestamp.
- Checksums (pre/post) for snapshot objects.
- Subprocessor deletion confirmation (where available).
- Audit log extract (time-ordered).

DocuSign / DPA draft: https://app.docusign.com/medshore/dpa-amendment-draft (preview)
Attachment: dpa_transfer_map_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

Regards,
Markus Klein
Senior Site Reliability Engineer

- Can Redwood commit to providing a per-wave deletion attestation signed by an authorized Redwood representative?
- For the subprocessor list, can you provide country of operation and a point of contact (email) so Legal can validate data flows?
- We need to confirm whether EU-origin logs stored by SubProcLogs Ltd will ever be transferred to US-based systems for restore or analysis. If yes, Legal wants the contractual mechanism (SCCs, BCRs, or adequacy statement) documented.

MedShore would also like a short, redlined DPA blurb for the backup purge section so we can attach it to our vendor assessment.

We can do a 30-minute call tomorrow; I'll defer to Laura for scheduling.

—Natalie
